bull.b: Strong data center and infrastructure demand supports multi-year growth in electrical protection, cooling and cable-management products. These applications are tied to expanding digital infrastructure and electrification investment, strengthening the company’s long-term market opportunity.

Product innovation and expanded manufacturing capacity improve nVent’s ability to capture fast-growing applications, particularly liquid cooling and AI infrastructure. Continued investment through 2027-2028 can support share gains and reduce capacity constraints as customer demand scales.

Robust free cash flow provides internally generated funding for capacity expansion, product development and shareholder returns. Improving leverage, available liquidity and targeted 90%-95% cash conversion also give nVent flexibility to manage investment needs without excessive balance-sheet strain.

bear.b: Higher tariffs and inflation can structurally pressure product costs and operating margins, especially while the company expands capacity and serves global supply chains. Recovery depends on pricing, sourcing and productivity actions, creating an ongoing earnings risk over the next several quarters.

Revenue growth has not fully translated into net profitability, while Electrical Connections margins remain exposed to inflation and mix. Sustained pressure would limit operating leverage and make future earnings increasingly dependent on execution, pricing and favorable business mix.

Large, uneven orders can make revenue and capacity planning volatile, while a mostly short-duration backlog limits long-term visibility. Simultaneous facility ramps also add labor, equipment and supplier risks that could delay benefits or pressure incremental margins.
